articles.title: Veja como foi o debate com os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão na TV Mirante
articles.summary: Participam os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.
articles.body:
Participam os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.

Debate foi realizado na terça-feira (29) e foi mediado pelo jornalista Hélter Duarte, da TV Globo.

Participaram os candidatos André Luís (Missão), Eduardo Braide (PSD), Felipe Camarão (PT), Orleans Brandão (MDB), Roberto Rocha (PRTB) e Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU).

Encontro teve mais de duas horas de duração com quatro blocos, sendo dois de tema livre e dois de tema determinado, além das considerações finais.

O g1 agradece a audiência durante o debate entre os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão. Até a próxima cobertura!

Fim do debate entre os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

O sexto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Orleans Brandão (MDB).

O quinto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é André Luís (Missão).

O quarto candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Felipe Camarão (PT).

O terceiro candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Roberto Rocha (PRTB).

O segundo candidato a fazer suas considerações finais é Eduardo Braide (PSD).

Começam as considerações finais. O primeiro candidato a falar é Saulo Arcangeli (PSTU). A ordem foi definida em sorteio.

Início do quarto e último bloco do debate.

Começa o debate com os candidatos ao governo do Maranhão na TV Mirante. Acompanhe!

Tudo pronto para começar o debate com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

Em entrevista, o candidato Eduardo Braide (PSD) falou sobre a expectativa para o debate e afirmou que o encontro será uma oportunidade para que os candidatos apresentem suas propostas. Ele também destacou temas como segurança pública e saúde como prioridades para o Maranhão.

"Uma expectativa que eu acho que é de todo o Maranhão poder acompanhar as propostas de cada candidato, o que pensa cada um, o que já fez cada um. Eu tenho certeza que será uma grande noite da democracia. Acho que as propostas é o que deve prevalecer hoje, para que o povo do Maranhão possa avaliar aquele que está mais preparado, que tem mais condições de cuidar da vida de 7 milhões de maranhenses a partir do ano que vem. E, sem sombra de dúvidas, segurança, saúde, algo que qualquer maranhense clama pela discussão desses dois temas. Eu tenho certeza que serão dois temas abordados no debate de hoje", diz o candidato.

O candidato Eduardo Braide (PSD) foi o último a chegar aos estúdios da TV Mirante para o debate com candidatos ao governo do Maranhão.

articles.title: Debate pelo governo do TO chega ao fim; veja os destaques
articles.summary: Participam do debate Laurez Moreira (PSD), Professor Witer Naves (PSOL), Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).
articles.body:
Participam do debate Laurez Moreira (PSD), Professor Witer Naves (PSOL), Professora Dorinha (União) e Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB).

Debate ocorreu nesta terça-feira (29), depois da novela Quem Ama Cuida, da TV Globo.

Programa foi dividido em quatro blocos com temas livres e determinados por sorteio, além de um bloco destinado às considerações finais.

No primeiro e no terceiro blocos, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres.

No segundo e no quarto, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo.

Encerrado o debate realizado pela TV Anhanguera com os candidatos ao governo do Tocantins. Reveja os vídeos do programa.

Vicentinho Júnior (PSDB) encerra a rodada de considerações.

Agora é a vez da Professora Dorinha (União) fazer sua conclusão.

Laurez Moreira (PSD) faz suas considerações finais.

Candidatos iniciam as considerações finais. A ordem também foi definida em sorteio. O primeiro é o Professor Witer Naves (PSOL).

Quarto bloco finalizado. Em instantes, candidatos farão suas considerações finais.

Chegamos agora ao último bloco do programa. As perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez. Ao final, cada um terá um tempo reservado para fazer suas considerações finais.

Começa o terceiro bloco do debate. Assim como no primeiro, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Fim do segundo bloco. Voltamos em instantes.

Começa o segundo bloco. Neste momento, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo. Cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Fim do primeiro bloco. Voltamos em instantes.

Começa o debate. Neste primeiro bloco, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. A ordem das perguntas foi definida em sorteio. Em todos os blocos, cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez.

Vicentinho Júnior explicou o que espera do debate.

"Hoje é o último debate do primeiro turno. Então é como eu tenho dito durante todos os outros debates que fizemos, as oportunidades que nos foram dadas, eu vou tratar esse momento eleitoral com muito respeito, vou aproveitar esse momento rico de um horário nobre pra mim me apresentar mais uma vez, apresentar as nossas propostas que até aqui nos trouxe a caminhada do 45. Continuarei a respeitar as pessoas, a respeitar a matéria humana e tô pronto pra um bom debate, a como me for chamado. Então, o tocantinense conhece o jeito do Vicentinho Júnior de ser, um homem respeitoso, um homem cauteloso, mas um homem que sempre fez o bom enfrentamento quando necessário foi. Então, hoje, em um último programa, eu não posso ser diferente disso, a não ser um candidato que quer mostrar ao povo tocantinense que a verdadeira mudança é que faz bem".

Laurez também falou sobre sua expectativa para o debate.

"A expectativa é muito boa. Eu sempre tenho o maior prazer de fazer com que as pessoas me conheçam o máximo. Porque quem conhece a história de Laurez Moreira, o seu passado, o legado que eu tenho deixado por onde eu tenho passado, sempre me apoia, né? Eu tenho certeza de que eu quero que o povo do estado do Tocantins, todos me conheçam e conheçam bem a minha essência como homem, como pai de família, como político e a pessoa que sempre tá na política por vocação e por vontade de servir a nossa gente. Eu espero que as pessoas possam fazer uma avaliação melhor de todos os candidatos, para conhecer o perfil, o que que pensa, a maneira de agir de cada um".

Professora Dorinha (União Brasil) falou de sua expectativa para o debate.

"Eu acho que é uma oportunidade que a imprensa tanto dá para o candidato, no meu caso, a candidata, falar sobre as propostas, projetos, como enxerga, é, o estado, quanto para o eleitor avaliar e comparar candidatos, comparar propostas. É, eu acho que, dentro da estrutura democrática do nosso país, a imprensa cumpre um papel extremamente importante. Então, é um debate muito esperado durante a campanha toda, né? E a minha expectativa é que a gente possa discutir projeto, ideia, modelo do estado."

Witer Naves (PSOL) falou sobre a expectativa para o debate.

"Tem uma importância histórica do campo democrático, e a gente acredita que esse debate hoje, ele constrói, sem dúvida alguma, alguns marcos para o domingo. Então, domingo a gente tem a aquilo que a gente ao longo de todo o processo está construindo, mas que sem dúvida alguma, a TV Globo, a sua afiliada TV Anhanguera ajudou na história do Brasil a construir, que foi a tomada de decisão significativamente, a tomada de decisão do eleitor aqui do Tocantins e do Brasil".

O debate será dividido em quatro blocos, com perguntas feitas entre os próprios candidatos. Em todos os blocos, cada candidato terá direito a fazer uma pergunta e a responder uma vez. No primeiro e no terceiro blocos, os candidatos poderão abordar temas livres. Já no segundo e no quarto, as perguntas serão sobre temas definidos pela produção e sorteados ao vivo.

Os tempos serão os mesmos em todos os blocos. O candidato que fizer a pergunta terá 30 segundos para formulá-la e 1 minuto e 15 segundos para a réplica. Quem responder terá 3 minutos e 15 segundos, que poderão ser divididos entre a resposta e a tréplica.

A ordem das perguntas de cada bloco foi sorteada previamente, na presença de representantes dos candidatos. Ao final do quarto bloco, cada candidato terá um tempo reservado para fazer suas considerações finais.

Boa noite. A TV Anhanguera realiza nesta terça-feira (29) o debate com candidatos ao governo do Tocantins. O programa será exibido logo após a novela Quem Ama Cuida, da TV Globo. O g1 transmite ao vivo.

articles.title: Candidatos ao governo de MT participam de debate na TV Centro América; acompanhe ao vivo
articles.summary: Participam do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).
articles.body:
Participam do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).

Debate é realizado nesta terça-feira (29), nos estúdios da TV Centro América.

Foram convidados os candidatos cujos partidos tiveram representação de, no mínimo, cinco parlamentares eleitos no Congresso Nacional em 2022.

Programa é dividido em quatro blocos com temas livres e determinados por sorteio.

Termina o debate. Candidatos trocaram acusações e apresentaram propostas para saúde, violência contra mulher, administração pública, entre outros; leia mais aqui

Candidatos fazem as considerações finais.

Começa o quarto e último bloco do debate.

Candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso já estão posicionados no estúdio da TV Centro América para o início do debate!

Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) foi o terceiro candidato a chegar para o debate. Ele afirmou que se sente preparado caso seja eleito.

"Minha expectativa é me comunicar com o povo de Mato Grosso, debater sobre ideias, sobre projetos. Represento um modelo de gestão que vem dando certo em Mato Grosso e o meu dever é fazer cada vez melhor. Um novo ciclo que se inicia em janeiro, me sinto preparado e pronto para isso. Vou pedir ao povo que confie em mim, que eu vou honrar a confiança".

Doutora Natasha (PSD) foi a segunda candidata a chegar para o debate. Ela disse que as expectativas são as melhores possíveis.

“A gente tem uma expectativa muito positiva, muito grande mesmo, tendo em vista que estamos virando em cima dos candidatos que se mostraram à frente o tempo todo da campanha. Então, é um momento muito importante, além de se apresentar, falar das nossas propostas e estar em contato com nossos eleitores".

O candidato Wellington Fagundes (PL) foi o primeiro a chegar. Para ele, o debate é uma oportunidade da população conhecer suas propostas.

"Que a democracia vença, a liberdade de cada um de ir e vir, que seja implantada neste país. E por isso nós acreditamos muito que esse debate é uma oportunidade para que toda a população saiba do governo Wellington Fagundes, um governo humano, para cuidar das pessoas que vivem, que constroem o nosso estado de Mato Grosso".

O debate com candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso começa logo após a novela "Quem Ama Cuida", às 21h15. Confira as regras:

O debate terá quatro blocos . Em dois, as perguntas serão de tema livre; nos outros dois, os temas serão determinados.

As perguntas serão feitas de um candidato para outro. Todos terão oportunidade de perguntar e responder . A ordem de abertura de cada bloco foi definida por sorteio.

Em cada rodada, o candidato terá 30 segundos para fazer a pergunta . O candidato escolhido terá até 3 minutos e 30 segundos, divididos entre a resposta e a tréplica.

Quem fez a pergunta terá 1 minuto e 30 segundos para a réplica .

Ao fim do quarto bloco, cada candidato fará suas considerações finais .

A TV Centro América realiza o debate com os candidatos ao governo de Mato Grosso, na terça-feira (29), a partir das 22h15.Participarão do debate os candidatos Dra. Natasha (PSD), Otaviano Pivetta (Republicanos) e Wellington Fagundes (PL).

O mediador será o jornalista e apresentador Cleto Kipper. O g1 Mato Grosso vai transmitir ao vivo, acompanhe!

Inicialmente, estava previsto um debate com outros dois concorrentes, porém Ronaldo Mansur (PSOL) não pôde participar, pois sofreu um acidente, e Jerônimo Rodrigues (PT) optou por não comparecer.
articles.summary: Candidato ao governo foi entrevistado pela TV Bahia nesta terça-feira (29). Inicialmente, estava previsto um debate com outros dois concorrentes, mas eles não compareceram.
articles.body:
O candidato ao governo da Bahia ACM Neto ( União Brasil ) foi entrevistado pela TV Bahia, nesta terça-feira (29). O programa foi transmitido ao vivo pela emissora e pelo g1 , com apresentação da jornalista Zileide Silva , da TV Globo. As perguntas foram sorteadas na hora.

A TV Bahia promoveria um debate entre os postulantes a chefe do Executivo baiano, mas Ronaldo Mansur ( PSOL ) não pôde participar, pois está hospitalizado após um acidente de carro , e Jerônimo Rodrigues ( PT ) cumpriu agenda externa de campanha e optou por não comparecer.

ACM Neto começou sua participação prestando solidariedade ao candidato Ronaldo Mansur e, em seguida fez críticas a Jerônimo Rodrigues, por faltar ao confronto de ideias com ele. As cobranças seguiram até o fim da entrevista, em temas distintos, como segurança pública, saúde e educação.

Questionado sobre segurança pública, ACM Neto falou sobre as medidas que espera implantar com a governadoria da segurança, um dos seus principais projetos de campanha para o setor.

ACM Neto em entrevista na TV Bahia — Foto: Alan Oliveira/g1

Com relação à educação, o candidato se comprometeu a proporcionar uma transformação da qualidade de ensino no estado. Também garantiu que, caso seja eleito, vai manter programas já implantados pelo governo atual, como o "Pé de Meia" e o "Bolsa Presença", que têm como objetivo garantir permanência, presença e a conclusão escolar de estudantes.

Disse ainda que quer proporcionar para os adolescentes e jovens uma educação que torne a escola mais atrativa para o aluno.

Em seguida, o candidato se comprometeu a governar a Bahia com qualquer que seja o presidente eleito pelo povo e ao lado dos prefeitos de cada uma das 417 cidades do estado, independentemente do seu partido.

Com relação à saúde, ACM Neto voltou a se comprometer com o impedimento de aumentos no valor de contribuição do servidor público ao Plano de Saúde dos Servidores Públicos Estaduais da Bahia (Planserv). Citou ainda suas propostas para proporcionar melhorias na chamada fila da regulação.

"Quero, nesse momento, me dirigir a vocês que acompanharam essa entrevista, fazendo uma pergunta: 'Quem tem mais chance de resolver os problemas da Bahia? Um governador que prometeu, há quatro anos atrás, zerar a fila da regulação, enfrentar o crime, melhorar a qualidade da educação e fazer a Bahia crescer, e nada disso aconteceu, ou eu, que fui [por] oito anos considerado o melhor prefeito das capitais brasileiras, que saí com mais de 80% de aprovação, que rodei todo esse estado, que tenho um amor enorme pela Bahia?'. Eu quero fazer história, eu quero permitir que a Bahia tenha o melhor governo de todo o Brasil. Eu garanto: 'Vocês não vão se decepcionar comigo'. Jerônimo já teve a chance dele. Eu, agora, peço a sua chance. Então, dia 4 de outubro, por favor, confia na gente, votem 44 e vamos mudar a Bahia", disse.

articles.title: SIR on duty, just not for studies: Full academic year may be at risk
articles.summary: Election duty leaves Delhi govt teachers juggling classes and Special Intensive Revision voter verification till Dec, raising fears of disrupted teaching and exams.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With teachers juggling classrooms and election work for months, educators fear their continuing deployment could end up taking a toll on an entire academic year in some govt schools.What began as a time-bound exercise has stretched through crucial months of teaching, and with SIR-related work expected to continue till Dec, school heads say managing regular classes, examinations and evaluation alongside field duties is becoming increasingly difficult.“The entire academic year is getting affected,” said a govt school principal. “If teachers continue with this work till Dec and Census-related work begins after that, when the entire staff may again be involved, then when will teaching happen?”A large number of teachers serving as booth-level officers (BLOs) are balancing their regular school responsibilities with work related to Election Commission’s Special Intensive Revision (SIR).Their duties have expanded further following a change in the verification process for voters who could not be traced or whose records showed discrepancies. BLOs will now have to visit such voters at their homes, collect the required documents and upload them for scrutiny by the electoral registration officer, rather than requiring these cases to be resolved through in-person hearings.According to the head of a school in northwest Delhi, teachers deployed for the exercise are now expected to remain engaged till Dec, although the work had initially been expected to conclude around Oct. He added that while officially the directions state that work has to be done “beyond school hours”, it was impossible to manage along with regular classes.“In my school, I have given them relaxation for half the day. They remain in school till around 11am and we schedule their periods accordingly. After that, they leave for this work,” he said. But elsewhere, he added, teachers are expected to remain in school until 1pm or 2pm before beginning field visits.“A teacher works in school till 11am, noon or even 2pm, then goes into the field and works there till 6pm or 7pm. After that, there is uploading work at night. They are doing this on Saturdays and Sundays as well,” the principal said, adding that the loss of even one teacher can be especially difficult at the senior secondary level, where a school may have only one person teaching a specialised subject.Another school head said 34 teachers from his school had earlier spent more than 40 days on full-time BLO duty. Even when teachers are asked to keep election work outside school hours, that boundary does not always hold. “They come to us at noon or 1pm and say they have to go to the field,” he said. “It is at the cost of studies.”School heads are also being drawn into the exercise. The northwest Delhi principal said 53 principals in his zone had recently been assigned SIR-related duties after a notification at the end of Sept.Meanwhile, teachers remain answerable both to their schools and to election officials. articles.title: Florida officials have cleared the way for a $100 million-plus surf park where developers plan a 35-acre attraction with a six-acre artificial wave lagoon and half-mile beach miles from the ocean
articles.summary: A major new attraction is moving forward in Wesley Chapel, Florida, bringing the possibility of ocean-style surfing to a community located miles from the
articles.body: A major new attraction is moving forward in Wesley Chapel, Florida, bringing the possibility of ocean-style surfing to a community located miles from the coast. According to the Pasco County Community Website, Pasco County commissioners voted 3-0 in September to approve a comprehensive plan amendment and rezoning connected to the Two Rivers development. The approval clears an important land-use hurdle for Peak Surf Park, a proposed $100 million-plus project expected to include a 35-acre destination, a six-acre artificial wave lagoon and a half-mile sandy beach. Developers are targeting a late 2027 opening, although additional permits and construction milestones still need to be completed. Read on to know more here:A surf park in Wesley ChapelPeak Surf Park is planned along State Road 56 near U.S. 301, on the eastern side of the large Two Rivers development closest to Zephyrhills. Although the attraction would be far from the Gulf of Mexico, its central feature is designed to create the feeling of surfing at the beach. Visitors would enter a large artificial lagoon where mechanical equipment would generate waves for people with different levels of experience.The project would use Surf Lakes technology, developed in Australia. At the centre of the lagoon, a large plunger would move up and down to push waves outward in several directions at the same time. This design is intended to create different surf breaks around the lagoon, allowing beginners and experienced surfers to use the same facility during a session.Project details reviewed during the county approval process indicate that the lagoon could accommodate as many as 200 surfers per hour. Each surfer is expected to catch about 10 waves per session. That would give visitors more opportunities to practise than they might find at a crowded natural beach, where wave conditions can change quickly and access is often limited.More than a wave poolThe proposed attraction would be designed as a complete entertainment and lifestyle destination rather than a facility focused only on surfing. Plans call for a half-mile sandy beach around the lagoon, along with restaurants, bars, retail shops, fitness facilities and wellness spaces. An outdoor venue for concerts and other events is also included in the broader concept.The lagoon alone would require roughly eight million gallons of water. According to the project information, the water would be pumped into the facility over a period of two to three weeks. That detail has become one of the most closely watched parts of the proposal, especially because Pasco County faced water-use restrictions during an extreme water shortage earlier this year.Developer Tony Miller, a longtime Tampa-area surfer, has reportedly spent about two years working to secure the site and move the concept through the approval process. The project is being promoted as a way to bring consistent surfing conditions to the Tampa Bay region, which has warm weather and a large population but no dependable natural surf.Concerns over water and growthThe approval was not without opposition. During public meetings, residents raised concerns about water consumption, flooding, traffic, wildlife habitat and the loss of open land. More than a dozen people spoke against aspects of the proposal at a July planning hearing, questioning whether the surf park and the wider Two Rivers expansion could place too much pressure on local roads and utilities.The surf park is part of a much larger development plan covering 3,405 acres along State Road 56 between Morris Bridge Road and Gall Boulevard. Earlier versions of the plan included thousands of homes, apartments, townhomes and villas, as well as a hotel, an assisted living facility and approximately 1.3 million square feet of retail space.That scale means the future attraction cannot be viewed separately from the wider growth of the area. A popular surf park could bring visitors, jobs and new businesses, but it could also contribute to traffic and increase demand for water and public services. How those pressures are managed will likely remain a major issue as the project moves through later stages.Housing linked to the projectCounty commissioners attached a condition to the approval that connects a portion of the proposed housing to the surf park’s progress. Under the condition, the developer may add up to 240 garden-style apartments, but construction on those units cannot begin until Peak Surf Park receives its certificate of occupancy or three years have passed after the land-use amendment takes effect, whichever comes first.The condition gives the county a way to tie residential development to the delivery of the promised attraction. In practical terms, the project must reach a defined stage before the developer can move ahead with that part of the housing plan. Supporters may view the requirement as a safeguard, while opponents may argue that it does not address all of the broader infrastructure concerns linked to the Two Rivers buildout.Technology still facing a major testAlthough Surf Lakes has operated its wave-generating system at a lake in Yeppoon, Queensland, the technology has not yet been used at a fully operational commercial surf park where customers pay to ride. That makes the Wesley Chapel proposal particularly significant for the company and the emerging surf-park industry.Peak Surf Park could become one of the first paying venues to rely on the system. The success of the attraction will depend not only on the quality and consistency of the waves, but also on construction costs, safety, operating expenses and whether visitors are willing to pay for repeated sessions.County approval establishes the land-use framework, but it does not mean construction has begun. Developers still need to complete additional permitting and design work before breaking ground. The late 2027 opening target remains possible, although the schedule could change depending on approvals, financing, construction progress and the performance of the wave technology.If completed as planned, Peak Surf Park would give residents and visitors a place to surf without travelling to the ocean. It could become a distinctive new destination for Wesley Chapel and the wider Tampa Bay region, while also testing whether artificial wave attractions can succeed in rapidly growing communities far from the coast.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jornaleiros resistem às mudanças do mercado e mantêm bancas abertas | G1
articles.standfirst: No Dia do Jornaleiro, profissionais falam sobre o impacto das mudanças no consumo de informações e das adaptações necessárias para seguir com os negócios em Sorocaba (SP).
articles.summary: No Dia do Jornaleiro, profissionais de Sorocaba revelam como adaptaram as bancas de jornal para sobreviver à era digital e manter o público fiel.
articles.body:
🗞️📰 Se, no passado, era necessário procurar um jornaleiro para comprar o jornal e saber das manchetes “fresquinhas”, hoje, não é mais preciso sequer sair de casa para ficar informado sobre aquilo que acontece na cidade e no mundo. A tecnologia e a internet trouxeram mudanças para o consumo de informações e isso impactou diretamente as bancas. Enquanto a maioria desapareceu, algumas resistiram às transformações do mercado e seguem abertas, com um público cativo.

Para marcar o Dia do Jornaleiro , celebrado em 30 de setembro, o g1 conversou com dois profissionais que continuam com bancas abertas em Sorocaba (SP). Mesmo admitindo as mudanças impostas pelo tempo, eles contaram não pensar em abandonar os negócios e até se preparam para o futuro.

A Banca da Sé, que está há 78 anos na praça Coronel Fernando Prestes, é administrada por Miguel Moreira Machado Júnior. Tudo começou com o pai dele, que instalou o negócio ali em julho de 1948, com uma estrutura modesta.

“Meu pai conheceu o distribuidor de revistas da época, que pediu para ele abrir um ponto de banca no centro de Sorocaba. Eu tinha 11 anos quando comecei a intercalar os estudos com o trabalho na banca. Ele me trouxe para ver se eu pegava gosto pela coisa, mas não queria interferir no meu livre arbítrio, sabia que era muito trabalhoso”, disse.

Só que Machado pegou gosto pelo negócio e foi ficando. Depois de terminar os estudos, optou por seguir na banca, onde trabalha há 56 anos e viu, ao longo dessas décadas, o mercado se transformar. “Antes do advento da internet, havia cerca de 450 bancas de rua em Sorocaba. Hoje, se tiver 10, é muito”.

Banca da Sé está aberta desde julho de 1948 na praça Coronel Fernando Prestes, em Sorocaba (SP) — Foto: Arquivo Pessoal/Reprodução

O jornaleiro quase acertou esse número. De acordo com a Secretaria do Empreendedorismo, da Microempresa e da Empresa de Pequeno Porte (Semepp) da Prefeitura de Sorocaba, restam 15 bancas em atividade no município . E, para se manter em atividade, muitas tiveram que diversificar os produtos oferecidos.

“Virou uma loja de conveniência. Eu coloquei doces, recarga de celular, vendo chips, bebidas e isso sustenta. Não teria como ficar só com jornais e revistas. Nos áureos tempos, a banca vendia, em média, 300 jornais por dia. Aos domingos, vendíamos 600 exemplares, chegamos a ultrapassar mil. Hoje, caiu bastante. A internet alterou muitos segmentos e ficaram aqueles que se adequaram”.

Além das mudanças do mercado, o negócio também sofreu impactos da pandemia de covid-19. Depois de meses fechada por conta das restrições, a Banca da Sé deixou de abrir para o público aos domingos e feriados. “Após esse período, alteramos para segunda a sexta, das 8h às 17h, e aos sábados, das 8h às 14h. Antes, o movimento já tinha diminuído, mas a gente insistia”, contou Machado.

Jornaleiros Miguel Machado e Ivo Rocha mantêm bancas em Sorocaba (SP) com diversificação de produtos e público cativo — Foto: Erick Rodrigues/g1

Mais do que afetar o hábito de consumo de notícias, a tecnologia permitiu uma modernização de sistemas e processos. Mas não na Banca da Sé, que não aderiu à internet e nem mesmo ao computador. Há mais de 70 anos, todo o controle financeiro é feito à mão, no caderno.

“A banca não é informatizada. É assim desde o tempo do meu pai. Está tudo marcado aqui [no caderno]. Não desliga, não cai a internet, qualquer dúvida sobre os fornecedores está aqui. Esse aqui é o meu computador”.

Sem internet e computador: na Banca da Sé, em Sorocaba (SP), o controle financeiro é feito no bom e velho caderno até hoje — Foto: Erick Rodrigues/g1

A internet e, mais especificamente, as redes sociais foram incorporadas à rotina da Banca Progresso, que é administrada por Ivo Silvério da Rocha desde 1992. O jornaleiro mantém perfis do negócio no Instagram e no Facebook, além de utilizar o WhatsApp para comunicação com os clientes.

“Tenho umas revistas que, quando chegam, eu coloco no Instagram e acabo alcançando o público que gosta, que está procurando. Dá um retorno muito bom publicar lá dizendo que o produto chegou. Hoje, é difícil quem não tenha rede social e, como são poucas bancas, acaba impulsionando”, explicou.

Convivendo com os clientes há 34 anos, na região da Vila Progresso, Rocha também teve que investir na venda de outros produtos para seguir com o negócio. “Hoje, eu trabalho também com brinquedos, lupas corretivas, doces, pilhas e até cola. Também tem a prestação de serviços, com recarga de celular e de passe de ônibus”.

Além dos clientes habituais, o jornaleiro vê uma renovação de público, impulsionada por figurinhas e pela busca por opções fora das telas.

“A criançada compra figurinhas e, depois, me reconhece como o tio da banca e acabo conhecido por eles também. Vai formando o público. Os mais jovens também buscam quadrinhos e mangás, algumas escolas estão pedindo gibis para incentivar a leitura. E é muito legal perceber que já vendi figurinhas para três gerações, do avô ao neto”, pontuou Rocha.

Na Banca Progresso, em Sorocaba (SP), figurinhas e gibis garantem renovação de público para o negócio — Foto: Erick Rodrigues/g1

O jornaleiro da Banca da Sé ainda pretende seguir no comando do negócio por mais alguns anos, mas já é acompanhado pelo filho, que pode assumir a banca no futuro.

“Eu tenho clientes aqui de 60 anos, que são fiéis e voltam por serem bem tratados. E, também, os mais novos, que conquistamos. Meus pais batalharam juntos, é essa homenagem que eu deixo para os dois e é isso que eu tento passar para o meu filho. Respeito, trabalho e persistência acima de tudo. Comércio é assim”, destacou Machado.

Na Banca Progresso, a renovação de público e o auxílio das redes sociais tornaram Rocha mais otimista sobre a continuidade do negócio. “Eu não me vejo fora da banca, mesmo diminuindo o ritmo. Eu sou otimista, porque tem a criança que vem e pega a revista, não quer procurar na internet. Ela pega o papel e isso resgata um pouco. O trabalho de jornaleiro é muito gratificante, a nostalgia que traz”, finalizou.

Trabalhando como jornaleiro há 34 anos, Ivo Silvério da Rocha não se vê longe da banca e é otimista sobre o futuro do negócio — Foto: Erick Rodrigues/g1

articles.title: Apple Pay launches in India; here's how to set it up and where you can use it
articles.summary: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India.
articles.body: Apple has officially launched Apple Pay in India. With this launch the company brings its secure and seamless payment system to iPhone, iPad and Apple Watch users, with Mac support coming soon. Apple Pay roll out in the country will enable users to pay in stores, apps, and on the web without typing PINs and OTPs marking a significant milestone in India’s fast-growing digital payments ecosystem. At launch, Apple Pay supports Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, enabling payments at thousands of merchants across India and anywhere NFC transactions are accepted globally.Apple also emphasised that privacy remains central to how Apple Pay functions. When a card is added, the actual card number is never stored on the device or Apple's servers, nor shared with merchants during a transaction. Instead, the system assigns a unique Device Account Number, which is encrypted and stored securely within the device's Secure Element — a certified, industry-standard chip built specifically to protect payment information.Apple Pay launched in India: How it works, and who can use itPresently, Apple Pay is exclusively available to customers holding Axis Bank-issued Visa and Mastercard credit cards, letting them add those cards to Apple Pay and use them at thousands of in-store and online merchants across India, as well as anywhere that accepts NFC transactions.Jennifer Bailey, Apple's vice president of Apple Pay and Apple Wallet, framed the launch as a natural fit for India's fast-growing digital economy, pointing to the country's dynamic, digitally savvy population that's increasingly embracing cashless payments while expecting strong security and privacy standards. She described Apple Pay's core value proposition as making everyday card payments easy, secure, and private — from a simple tap in stores without needing a separate app, PIN, or OTP, to checking out online without repeatedly re-entering payment details.How to set up and use Apple PayApple Pay is easy to set up. Customers can add a card directly to Apple Wallet via the latest version of the Axis Bank app. Alternatively, simply open the Wallet app on iPhone, tap the plus sign, and follow the steps to add an eligible card. Once a user adds a card to their Apple device, they can start using Apple Pay right away.Using Apple Pay in stores is seamless and easy. Simply double-click the side button or Home button; authenticate using Face ID, Touch ID, or a device passcode if prompted; and hold the top of the iPhone or display of the Apple Watch near the contactless reader to pay. When using Apple Pay, users will continue to earn the rewards and benefits offered by their cards.Where you can use itAt launch, Apple Pay will be accepted at millions of merchants across India, including Apple Store locations, Blinkit, Chaayos, Comet, Croma, Interflora, Ixigo, Le15 Patisserie, Reliance brands, Tata 1mg, and Zomato, among others. Apple has also partnered with several payment service providers, including Cashfree, JusPay, Mswipe, Paytm, PayU, Pine Labs, Razorpay, and Worldline, to extend Apple Pay's reach across their respective merchant networks, with more merchants and apps expected to be added over time.Globally, Apple Pay is now available in more than 90 countries and regions, working with over 11,000 bank and network partners worldwide — making India one of the more prominent recent additions to that global rollout.You use AI every day. articles.title: Google CEO Sundar Pichai 'agrees' to the call that technology companies need to innovate responsibly; says: As I shared today ...
articles.summary: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super
articles.body: Google CEO Sundar Pichai has joined the US President Donald Trump, Senate leaders, and other tech executives in signing the White House Accord on Super Intelligence, a landmark agreement aimed at ensuring safe and responsible development of advanced AI systems. The accord, alongside a Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities, sets out tangible steps for companies to adopt safeguards while continuing to deliver economic and scientific benefits. Pichai revealed that Google has invested hundreds of billions of dollars in the past two years across its AI stack, with more spending planned. He emphasized that the company is focused on building products that deliver real value for people and businesses, while also investing in local communities and strengthening public trust in technology.What Google CEO Sundar Pichai saidIn a post on X, Pichai described the meeting as an important conversation, confirming that Google had signed what he called the White House Accord on Super Intelligence. “Great to meet today with @POTUS, @JDVance, @SpeakerJohnsonand Administration + tech leaders. Important conversation and we signed today the White House Accord on Super Intelligence.As I shared today, Google has invested hundreds of billions in the last two years alone, with more to come, across the entire stack, to deliver benefits for America and the world. We’re working to build products that deliver real value for people and businesses, invest in local communities, and build trust in the technology.Industry also has to innovate responsibly. Google’s focused on building the right way, with appropriate testing, evaluations, red-teaming, and other safeguards against misuse and misalignment – and releasing models or products only after they’ve been thoroughly reviewed.We are committed to working with other industry leaders to establish norms and build public confidence. The White House Accord and the Joint Commitment on Frontier Responsibilities signed today is a solid basis for moving forward - it contains real tangible steps to promote safe development, while delivering the economic and scientific benefits of this technology,” wrote Pichai in a post on X.What the accord actually saysThe full agreement is titled "The White House Accord on Superintelligence: Joint Commitment on Frontier SI Responsibilities." Beyond Pichai, it was signed by Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, OpenAI President Greg Brockman, xAI founder Elon Musk, and Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, alongside Trump himself.The one-page document lays out what's being described as a four-layer framework of controls and audits for frontier AI systems. The first layer requires companies to build robust internal processes to monitor their models during both training and deployment, ensuring systems behave as intended and that problems are identified and resolved quickly. Subsequent layers call for internal verification, partnerships with independent external auditors to assess whether safety controls are functioning as intended, and board-level oversight of the entire process.Voluntary, not legally bindingDespite its formal tone, House Speaker Mike Johnson was clear that the accord is entirely voluntary, and Trump himself described it as "morally" binding rather than legally enforceable, emphasizing that the industry will largely be left to police itself. At the signing event, Trump likened the document to a kind of constitution for AI governance, while Musk described the substance of the commitment as involving joint monitoring, special board committees, and companies essentially reviewing each other's safety practices.Zuckerberg struck a similarly measured tone afterward, calling the accord a reasonable starting point — one the broader industry could plausibly coalesce around going forward, rather than a finished framework.You use AI every day. articles.title: Video: BMC worker killed, 2 injured after ex-MP’s speeding car hits scooters in Mumbai
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday, with
articles.body: MUMBAI: A BMC employee was killed and two others injured after a speeding car allegedly rammed into two scooters on CD Road in Khar West on Monday, with CCTV footage capturing the crash.Police have registered an FIR against retired honorary Brigadier and former Rajapur MP Sudhir Sawant in connection with the incident.The CCTV footage shows the car hitting the scooters on the busy road, after which Iyappan Harijan, 41, was trapped underneath the vehicle. Bystanders lifted the car and pulled him out before he and his wife Nancy, 37, were taken to Bhabha Hospital in an autorickshaw.Harijan suffered severe injuries and repeatedly lost consciousness while being taken to hospital. He later died from blood loss.Nancy, who was riding pillion, suffered bruises on her left hand and other parts of her body. Another scooter rider, Rahul Ghanekar, suffered a fractured hand.Recalling the crash, Nancy said she saw her husband trapped beneath the car, with only his leg visible. People gathered at the spot and lifted the vehicle to pull him out. She said Harijan initially managed to sit up but had injuries to his head, face and other parts of his body.Khar police on Tuesday registered an FIR against Sawant, 71, under relevant Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita sections for causing death by negligence and rash and dangerous driving.Police said further action would be taken after Sawant is discharged from hospital. He was undergoing treatment after his blood pressure rose following the accident.According to Nancy’s complaint, the couple had left their home in Santacruz West around 4.15pm to shop in Bandra for an event at their home when the car allegedly hit their scooter from behind.Harijan had worked with MTNL for 16 years before joining BMC’s cleaning services department about a month ago. articles.body: BHOPAL: A retired IAS officer, Rakesh Agrawal, was allegedly found dead with his throat slit at his residence behind Panghat Colony in Suraj Nagar in Ratibad early Wednesday morning.A caretaker, who had reportedly been hired through an agency just four days ago, was found missing from the house.Police suspect the caretaker may have fled after the incident. articles.title: Suspect in alleged plot against British base called police before arrest, UK media report
articles.summary: One of the suspects in the alleged plot targeting a UK airbase used by the US military called the police shortly before they were arrested, multiple UK media outlets have reported.
articles.body: One of the suspects in the alleged plot targeting a UK airbase used by the US military called the police shortly before they were arrested, multiple British media outlets have reported. The five men were arrested early Sunday on suspicion of explosive offenses and later terrorism charges near a Royal Air Force base at Fairford in western England, from where US B-1 bombers have been flying missions against Iran. The incident triggered a major security response in the area and sparked alarm on both sides of the Atlantic, as well as accusations of foreign involvement. The five men were quickly released on bail and police have now confirmed no explosives were found in three vans at the scene, but the investigation remains ongoing. The latest revelation that one of the men called the police, was first reported by The Times of London, followed by the Guardian and the BBC, deepens the mystery. The Times and BBC both reported that the call from the suspect to 999, the emergency number used in Britain, came almost an hour before a female farmer alerted authorities after seeing a group of masked men and three white vans. The Times reported police were already on the scene when that later call from the local resident came in. The paper added police were investigating whether the suspect got cold feet or whether making such a call was part of the plan. In their latest public statements, British police have indicated there may have been more than one trigger that sparked them into action. “A police response was activated in the early hours of Sunday morning due to a range of information received, including a call from a member of the public about several vehicles acting suspiciously close to RAF Fairford,” Laurence Taylor, a senior counter-terrorism police officer, told reporters. Taylor said “no improvised explosive devices were found” in vehicles used by the men, but that “a quantity of petrol was recovered.” Police are planning to close down their investigative operations at Fairford by Wednesday, he added. The suspects, who have been identified only as British nationals aged between 23 and 25 from the London area, were released on bail Monday. Taylor defended the move as an “investigative decision” following criticism from US President Donald Trump, who said “I wouldn’t have done that.” US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Tuesday the suspected terror plot “clearly involved the hands of a foreign actor,” after Trump said the suspects “might be” connected to Iran. Iran has strongly denied any involvement. The UK has yet to publicly confirm any foreign link, though Taylor earlier said police were looking into it. Trump has suggested authorities were already looking into the group before the arrests were made - however UK authorities have not yet confirmed that.

articles.title: India’s Ujjain tense as mosque partially demolished for Hindu pilgrimage
articles.summary: Fearing outright demolition, Muslims volunteer to take down parts of the city’s Shahi Mosque themselves.
articles.body:
Zeeshan Khan says he has not slept properly for three nights in a row.

It began on Sunday when the 30-year-old joined hundreds of Muslims in central India’s Ujjain city for a night vigil outside a prominent mosque to prevent its partial demolition to widen the road for a Hindu pilgrimage festival held every 12 years.

Ujjain is about 200km (124 miles) from Bhopal, the capital of Madhya Pradesh state, which has been governed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) since 2003, barring a brief 15-month rule by the opposition Congress.

The Hindu nationalist BJP has been accused of a deliberate campaign to target Muslim religious structures – mosques, shrines, graveyards and madrasas (Islamic schools) – by claiming they were either illegally built or stood on former Hindu temples .

Hundreds of Muslim sites have been partially or fully demolished by the authorities in several BJP-governed states in recent years, many of them in the dead of night. In many cases, the demolitions took place even as the matter was still pending in courts.

The Muslim residents of Ujjain, who had similar fears of a nightly demolition, congregated outside the Shahi Mosque in Ujjain’s Chhatri Chowk area on Sunday night to protest against the planned demolition.

The government aims to clear and widen the road for Simhastha Kumbh Mela, a Hindu pilgrimage to be held on the banks of the Kshipra River in 2028.

“It started about two months ago, when the Ujjain Municipal Corporation issued a notice to the Shahi Masjid, saying that the mosque would have to be acquired because the road needed to be widened,” Khan, who runs a digital marketing business, told Al Jazeera on Tuesday over telephone.

He said the municipal authorities gave a September 10 deadline to “remove the structure ourselves”, failing which, the government would take strict action.

Meanwhile, a petition filed by the Muslims before the local High Court urging a halt to the demolition was dismissed, with the court saying the 2028 Hindu pilgrimage needs additional space to manage the traffic.

“Their argument was that a lot of people would be coming from outside and that the public should not face problems. So public interest had to come first,” Khan told Al Jazeera.

As protests continued, the mosque management held several rounds of discussions with the district authorities, forcing them to agree to three feet of space from the street to be removed instead of the more than seven feet of structure originally demanded by the officials.

On Sunday night, as the administration brought bulldozers near the mosque, thousands of people congregated at Chhatri Chowk. Authorities said AI-generated social media posts by some Muslim men caused rumours that the mosque was set to be demolished, triggering the night-long demonstration.

“But the administration blocked the area and told the community: ‘Either you demolish the mosque yourselves, or we will demolish it’,” said Khan.

As tension flared on Monday morning, the police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters. According to media reports, the demonstrators threw stones at the police, who launched a baton attack on the crowd, in which at least a dozen people were injured. Several men were also arrested.

Meanwhile, as fears of an outright bulldozer action on the mosque grew, the mosque committee agreed to remove a part of the structure themselves. Dozens of Muslim men began taking down the platform along the mosque, using hammers and rods.

“We demolished it with our own hands,” Khan said. “It hurts us deeply.”

On Tuesday, part of the mosque’s minaret was removed by the authorities, he added. “They started the demolition work on the minaret, but no such work has started inside the mosque yet.”

Authorities in Ujjain have sealed the area around the Shahi Mosque and deployed heavy security.

As Ujjain remained tense, a Muslim group held a protest on Tuesday in the national capital “against the continued action and demolition targeting mosques and places of worship”. Organised by the Monitoring Committee of Indian Muslims, the protesters included several Muslim parliamentarians and religious leaders.

“Our issue is much bigger than a single mosque or a single community. When a place of worship is demolished, or action is taken against it without ensuring legal and constitutional protections, it raises serious questions about the rule of law,” Syed Sadatullah Hussaini, president of Jamaat-e-Islami Hind, said in a statement.

Several calls made by Al Jazeera to two BJP spokespersons in Madhya Pradesh went unanswered.

Asif Mujtaba, founder of a New Delhi-based charity, told Al Jazeera that many Muslims connect demolition drives with the broader political environment in the country since the BJP came to power.

“People link these demolitions with the language used in politics, with campaigns around mosques, with pressure on madrasas and with repeated disputes around Muslim institutions,” he said.

“People see their history disappearing from the city.”

articles.title: Drumcree dispute: More talks taking place at Hillsborough
articles.summary: Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant is holding further talks with community leaders over the controversial Drumcree march.
articles.body:
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant is holding further talks with community leaders on Wednesday over the controversial Drumcree march.

It comes after lawyers for the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition issued a fresh legal bid to try to prevent the march from going ahead.

Members of the Orange Order are still waiting to begin their permitted parade, which was due to take place on Sunday, and walk down the mainly-nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown.

The residents' appeal will be the latest challenge to the march, which was given the go ahead after three separate legal hearings over the course of 13 hours late on Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday morning.

Wednesday's talks at Hillsborough Castle took place in an upstairs room which, under normal circumstances, is used as a sitting room.

The Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition and the Portadown Orange Order waited in separate rooms before going upstairs for talks.

What is the Garvaghy Road dispute all about?

Parading, policing and power sharing collide amid Drumcree dispute

Drumcree parade resolution not going to be easy - NI secretary

Senior members from the Orange Order, including Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson and Deputy District Master Alastair Power, met the secretary of state.

They were accompanied by loyalist activist Jamie Bryson, who has acted as an adviser for the lodge.

Speaking after their meeting, Dawson said the contents of the meetings remained "confidential".

But he added that the secretary of state had been left "in no doubt" that the Orange Order's position continued to be that he and the chief constable must apply the law to allow the march to take place.

Bryson was asked about what had happened and said while he did not want to speak for the Orange Order, "if the law is not applied how can the executive possibly survive?"

It is understood Bryson has not been part of the discussions with Sir Chris and has been waiting in a separate room.

Members of the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition, including Breandán Mac Cionnaith, also arrived to Hillsborough Castle on Wednesday morning.

Mac Cionnaith said little on the way in, and did not respond to a suggestion that he'd told residents last night that mediation was "dead in the water" .

When asked what his message would be to Sir Chris, he replied: "I think you know that."

The discussions are a form of proximity talks, with the two sides not meeting face-to-face but both being under the same roof.

Wednesday's discussions are the third day in a row that Hillsborough talks have taken place.

Dozens of protesters remain at the Garvaghy Road on Wednesday.

Paul and Charlie told BBC News NI that they have camped out for nearly 24 hours.

They said they were relieved to see the sun come out today after the "wild" weather overnight that saw the protest site battered by wind and rain.

Members of the Orange Order left Drumcree Church overnight - the first time since the standoff began. It's understood they left on health and safety reasons due to the adverse weather.

However, a small crowd returned this morning, where they continue to wait for news from the talks at Hillsborough.

There was another attempt by Portadown District Lodge to walk the route at 22:10 BST on Tuesday.

Accompanied by DUP MP Carla Lockhart, Power asked the police if they could facilitate their parade. The answer was no.

The Drumcree parade, which in the 1990s sparked some of the most serious disorder in Northern Ireland's history, was due to go ahead on Sunday for the first time in almost 30 years after a series of legal challenges.

Since 1998, the Orange Order had been banned from completing its Drumcree march - and until this year had been repeatedly refused permission to finish the route by the Parades Commission, which was set up to adjudicate disputes.

The Orange Order is a Protestant pro-British organisation, while the area where it wants to walk - specifically along the Garvaghy Road - is largely Catholic and predominantly inhabited by pro-Irish nationalists.

Both the Orange Order and members of the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition also met Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant at Hillsborough Castle on Tuesday.

Speaking on his way into the talks, Breandán Mac Cionnaith, from the Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition, said "reroute the sectarian parade, that's it".

Speaking after a separate meeting with the secretary of state, Portadown District Master Nigel Dawson said the talks had been "positive and constructive".

Later, hundreds of people attended a meeting beside St John the Baptist Church on the Garvaghy Road for an update on the talks process.

Speaking to the media outside the hall, Mac Cionnaith said the only person the residents had left to meet was PSNI Chief Constable Jon Boutcher.

He said he will be waiting for Boutcher to let him know when the meeting would happen, adding: "Or is he going to hide behind a wall of uniforms of police in riot gear?"

Meanwhile, the Portadown district master told hundreds of supporters at an outdoor rally in the town that unionist leaders needed to keep pressure on the secretary of state and chief constable and that the law must be "respected and applied".

Nigel Dawson said: "Tonight, my position, our position, is very, very clear. The chief constable, who is responsible for ensuring the law is complied in this country, must apply the law.

"He must respect the High Court judgement and he must deliver us safely and securely back to Carleton Street Orange Hall via the Garvaghy Road because that's what the Parade's Commission said and that is what a High Court has said.

Sinn Féin have called on the Irish government to intervene in the dispute.

The Orange Order, the most prominent of the loyal orders associated with Protestants in Northern Ireland, holds thousands of parades every year and the vast majority pass off without incident.

However, many Catholics see the marches as sectarian and object to them passing through, or close to, Catholic or nationalist areas.

The Garvaghy Road had been part of the Drumcree route, but by the mid 1990s nationalist residents protested against the parade. The row sparked some of the most serious public disorder in Northern Ireland's history and was linked to several murders.

The Drumcree dispute was one of Northern Ireland's most serious parading disputes during the 1990s, when stand-offs over attempts by the Orange Order to march along the Garvaghy Road were accompanied by riots, roadblocks and killings.

When the Orange Order was prevented by police from walking down the route in July 1995, there was a tense stand-off. It was the same for the next three years.

Violence related to the dispute resulted in riots, roadblocks and murders across Northern Ireland.

In 1998, the newly-established Parades Commission ruled that the Orange Order should not march down the road - a decision upheld for the last 28 years.

The row reemerged last month after a court case in which a ruling by the Parades Commission was overturned, and a fresh application was lodged.

On Friday, the commission decided the march could go ahead with restrictions in place. However that decision was challenged in several Belfast courts on Saturday, before finally being given the go ahead just hours before it was due to take place .

articles.title: Meet Dr Ejaz Ali: Patna doctor who charges just Rs 10 for consultation and has kept his fee unchanged for decades; asks doctors to ‘think of the patient’s pocket’
articles.summary: In Patna's Bikhna Pahari area, the scene outside Dr Ejaz Ali's hospital is markedly different from what many patients may expect from a senior surgeon.
articles.body: In Patna's Bikhna Pahari area, the scene outside Dr Ejaz Ali's hospital is markedly different from what many patients may expect from a senior surgeon. Instead of sitting inside an elaborate consultation room, Ali is often seen in a simple kurta-pyjama and skull cap, sitting on a plastic chair in the open courtyard of his hospital as patients wait for their turn. The consultation fee is Rs 10. Dr Ali has kept the fee at the same amount for decades. He began practicing as a general surgeon in Patna in 1984 and, according to a February 2025 TOI report, continues to see more than 100 patients on an average day and perform seven to eight surgeries. Patients also travel to his hospital from different parts of Bihar.The low-cost approach extends beyond consultation. According to an earlier TOI report, appendix operation at his hospital, including post-surgery medicines, costs around Rs 17,000, while gallbladder stone removal costs about Rs 11,000, including medicines. In some cases, surgery charges are waived, while patients who cannot pay at once may be allowed to pay in installments.Why has he kept the consultation fee at Rs 10?For Ali, the answer goes back to his own experience of poverty and the advice he received from his mother. When TOI asked him why he had kept his fee so low, he said, "I saw poverty around me and there were certain instructions from my mother too." He also explained why he tries to see patients on the same day. Many of those who come to his hospital travel from outside Patna, and another visit can mean additional spending on transport, food and accommodation. "I get satisfaction from such service to society," he said.From Patna Medical College to a decades-long medical practiceAli was born in 1958 into a lower-middle-class family and was one of 10 siblings. He studied medicine at Patna Medical College and Hospital and later completed his master's in surgery. He started his medical practice in Patna in 1984. His father, Sheikh Mumtaz Ali, worked as a Block Development Officer. His career later extended beyond medicine. Dr Ejaz Ali was elected to the Rajya Sabha from Bihar in March 2008. He served as a member of the Upper House until July 2010. During his parliamentary tenure, he raised issues relating to Bihar, minorities and access to government services, among other subjects.His advice to other doctorsDespite his long medical career, Ali's own approach to treatment remains focused on keeping the financial burden on patients in mind. His message to fellow doctors is, "Before treatment, think of the patient's pocket. Do not go for unnecessary tests and expensive medicines. One needs to get out of greed." His daughter Dr Suraiya Anjum, a gynaecologist, told TOI that her father's behaviour with patients has also influenced the family. "He is somebody who never raises his voice, never gets irritated. It is not easy to imbibe these habits," she said. His other daughter, Dr Naghma Anjum, is a pathologist. She described how the family has watched him continue working for long hours. "We get scolded, even if the patient is wrong, but patients are his priority. We have seen him operating for hours together, even while fasting with just one date. In fact, his support staff have also become like him, humble and hardworking."His late wife was also a doctor; three children followed the professionMedicine has remained a family profession for the Ali household. According to a TOI report, his late wife was also a doctor and charged only Rs 10 for her services. His three children are doctors as well. His son, who studied medicine at an American institution, charges Rs 100 for consultation, while his daughter Dr Suraiya Anjum charges Rs 50. The family's medical practice has therefore continued the principle of keeping consultation charges relatively low, although the fees charged by the children are different from their father's Rs 10 fee.A hospital that draws patients from across BiharAli's hospital in the Bikhna Pahari/Ashiana-Digha Road area has become a destination for patients looking for affordable treatment. People from different parts of Bihar travel to the hospital. On an average day, Ali sees large daily patient numbers at his clinic. Ali has also been involved in social and political activities. He has worked for the rights of disadvantaged communities and has been associated with the All-India Backward Muslim Morcha, which he founded in 1994. Decades after starting his practice, the routine remains simple: patients arrive, wait their turn, and meet a surgeon whose consultation fee is still Rs 10. For patients who have travelled from outside the city, Ali's decision to see them on the same day can also mean one less trip and fewer expenses. As he put it, "I get satisfaction from such service to society."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Israel-bound plane drops 17,000 feet after pilot reportedly stabbed
articles.summary: A Flydubai flight was diverted to Saudi Arabia after an apparent cockpit fight, as Israeli officials say it could be a terror attack attempt. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Hijacking attempt: Israeli sources told CNN they suspect the co-pilot of an Israel-bound Flydubai flight forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia tried to hijack the plane after stabbing the captain. It is unclear if the intention was to crash the jet or take hostages.

• Passenger’s fear: The incident caused the aircraft, traveling from Dubai to Tel Aviv, to plummet 17,400 feet in less than two minutes, flight tracking data shows. One passenger told Israeli media there were moments she believed she was going to die.

• Israel’s response: It also prompted Israel’s prime minister and defense minister to hold a security consultation . Separately, an official said Israel is exploring the possibility of sending a military or civilian plane to bring passengers home.

Two Israeli sources tell CNN they suspect the co-pilot of the Israel-bound Flydubai flight was trying to hijack the plane after stabbing the captain.

The sources said it was not yet clear whether the intention would have been to crash the plane or to land it and take hostages.

Both the pilot and co-pilot were injured in the incident on the flight which was traveling to Tel Aviv but forced to make an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia.

Photographs apparently taken aboard the diverted Flydubai flight show a male passenger in a bloodied t-shirt and jeans.

The two photos, circulating widely on social media, show the unidentified man sitting in his seat and standing up, seemingly uninjured, but with large blood stains on his clothes.

Several of those who were on the flight have told Israeli media that the attacker was subdued by the passengers after stabbing the pilot.

A host of Israeli agencies, including Shin Bet, Mossad, the military and the country’s transportation ministry, are involved in investigating the Flydubai incident that took place this morning, an Israeli official told CNN.

One of the main questions being looked into is why the flight crew included a pilot from a country with which Israel does not have diplomatic relations, the official said.

One of the pilots on Flydubai flight FZ1073 was Omani , two Israeli officials told CNN earlier. One of the officials said the Omani national was the co-pilot, allegedly the attacker in the violent incident.

Oman and Israel do not have formal diplomatic relations. It is not yet clear how the Omani pilot would have obtained clearance to fly to Israel.

CNN’s Jeremy Diamond and Catherine Nicholls contributed to this reporting.

The mother of a passenger on board Flydubai flight FZ1073 said that her daughter told her the pilot of the aircraft was stabbed.

The pilot was “screaming ‘help, help, help’,” Yasmin Abukasi told the Reuters news agency.

“She said it’s crazy, crazy time. It’s very hard to explain what’s happened there, but it was big stress. And after the plane start to go down, and they thinks they’re going to (crash) and now they land in Saudi, the people (are) in stress and shock,” she said.

Footage from the diverted Israel-bound Flydubai flight posted on social media shows passengers celebrating as the plane lands in Saudi Arabia.

People in the video can be seen clapping, chanting and cheering as the aircraft touches down at Tabuk Airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia.

The aircraft dropped more than 17,000 feet, according to tracking data reviewed by CNN, after a “violent incident” broke out between the pilots.

The captain and co-pilot of the diverted flight were both injured in this morning’s incident and taken to hospital, Saudi Arabia’s leading aviation operator Cluster2 said in a statement .

Meanwhile, a passenger told Israel’s i24 channel that there were moments she believed she was going to die.

CNN’s Eyad Kourdi, Catherine Nicholls, Dana Karni and Ivana Kottasová contributed reporting.

Flydubai is wholly owned by the Dubai government, which established the airline in 2008 through the Dubai Aviation Corporation.

Operating from Dubai International Airport, the airline serves 131 destinations including to the Middle East, Europe, Africa and Asia.

Flydubai is often considered as the low-cost sister carrier to the United Arab Emirates’ (UAE) Emirates airline. It is a separate entity, although both ultimately share the same owner - the Dubai government, via its sovereign wealth fund, the Investment Corporation of Dubai.

Currently, the airline’s fleet consists of variations of the Boeing 737 aircraft.

The airline has maintained a solid safety record since its establishment. Its only fatal incident was in March 2016, when a flight from Dubai to Rostov-on-Don, Russia, crashed during a landing attempt amid high ground-level wind and poor visibility. All 62 passengers and crew members on board were killed.

More details are beginning to emerge surrounding this morning’s incident aboard Flydubai flight FZ1073, which was traveling from Dubai in the United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv in Israel.

Israeli authorities suspect the Flydubai incident may have been an attempted terrorist attack , two Israeli officials and an Israeli source familiar with the situation said.

An Israeli official told CNN that information gathered suggests the co-pilot tried to stab the pilot , and a passenger helped to take him down.

The captain and co-pilot of the plane were both injured in the incident and taken to hospital, Saudi Arabia’s leading aviation operator said.

One of the pilots on Flydubai flight FZ1073 was Omani , two Israeli officials told CNN. One of the officials said the Omani national was the co-pilot, who was allegedly the attacker.

We’ll bring you more on this as we get it.

CNN’s Tal Shalev, Jeremy Diamond, Dana Karni, Ivana Kottasová and Eyad Kourdi contributed to this reporting.

One of the pilots on Flydubai flight FZ1073 was Omani, two Israeli officials told CNN.

One of the officials said the Omani national was the co-pilot, who was alledegly the attacker in the violent incident that took place aboard the plane.

Here is the timeline of the diverted Flydubai Flight FZ1073, based on publicly available data:

6:05 a.m. Flight FZ1073 takes off from Dubai and flies west.

8:20 a.m. The plane begins losing altitude and turns sharply to the north. It descends 17,400 feet in just under two minutes.

8:31 a.m. The flight issues a distress call by squawking code 7700, the International Civil Aviation Organization code for emergency.

8:35 a.m. The flight squawks code 7500, which signals aircraft hijacking.

8:41 a.m. The plane turns around and enters Jordanian airspace.

8:46 a.m. The plane re-enters Saudi airspace.

9:54 a.m. Flight FZ1073 touches down at Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport.

The captain and co-pilot of the diverted Flydubai flight FZ1073 were both injured in this morning’s incident and taken to hospital, Saudi Arabia’s leading aviation operator Cluster2 said in a statement a short while ago.

The Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport in Tabuk received a distress call from the Flydubai plane requesting an emergency landing at the airport at 8:44 a.m. local time this morning (1:44 a.m. ET), it said.

The airport declared a state of emergency, and the plane landed safely just over an hour later, it continued.

Both the plane’s captain and co-pilot were transferred to hospital because of their injuries, the aviation operator said, while passengers were treated in the airport terminal.

Coordination has also been carried out to arrange a replacement aircraft following this morning’s incident, Cluster2 said.

Dubai - from where the diverted Israel-bound flight was returning - has become one of Israel’s busiest and most frequently served international destinations.

This is thanks to the normalization of relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) in 2020, through the brokered Abraham Accords , which allowed commercial aviation services between the two countries to resume.

Since then, the aviation corridor between Ben Gurion Airport (TLV) and Dubai International Airport (DXB) has seen significant growth, with both Israel- and UAE-based airlines expanding operations to meet the demand for tourism and business travel.

According to flight tracking website FlightRadar24, there are typically 70 flights running between Dubai (DXB) and Tel Aviv (TLV) per week. Flydubai is the main carrier operating the route, in addition to Emirates and Israeli airlines Israir and El Al.

Data from Israel’s Ben Gurion Airport in December showed that 1.1 million Israeli passengers traveled to Dubai in 2025.

A passenger on board the Flydubai flight told Israel’s i24 channel that one of the pilots on the flight was stabbed and there were moments she believed she was going to die.

“We just heard screams, and then the cockpit door opened and we saw a huge amount of blood,” the passenger, identified only as Miriam, told the channel.

She said one of the pilots was injured and was receiving first aid but it was unclear who stabbed them.

She said the plan was “completely out of control.”

There has been no confirmation of what happened on board the flight but an Israeli official told us that information gathered suggests the co-pilot tried to stab the pilot, and a passenger helped to take him down.

Israeli authorities suspect the Flydubai incident may have been an attempted terrorist attack, two Israeli officials and an Israeli source familiar with the situation said.

One of the officials said that information gathered by Israeli authorities indicates that the co-pilot tried to stab the pilot, and an Israeli passenger helped restrain the co-pilot.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cancelled his schedule to hold consultations with Israel’s top security officials about the incident, the source said.

The footage above, from Flightradar24, shows Flydubai Flight FZ1073 head to Tel Aviv from Dubai diverted over Jordanian airspace towards Saudi Arabia.

The plane, according to the flight tracking data, veers off its path to fly into Jordanian airspace, then loops back on itself to re-enter Saudi airspace, instead of traveling onwards to Israel.

Earlier today, sources told CNN that the Flydubai aircraft was diverted following a “violent incident” between two pilots. An Israeli official said the incident was not a hijacking and that the plane has now landed.

While we establish exactly what happened on this morning’s Flydubai flight, let’s look at some previous incidents in which fights have broken out between crew members.

In June 2022, two Air France pilots were involved in an inflight altercation and exchanged “inappropriate gestures” while in the cockpit of an A320 heading from Geneva to Paris, the airline said. The spat led to the suspension of both pilots.

In January 2018, it was reported that two Indian pilots were fired after they fought inside a cockpit during a flight from London to Mumbai operated by private airline Jet Airways. The fight broke out when the male pilot slapped the female pilot, according to reports, and the cockpit was left unattended twice during the incident.

Two Iraqi Airways pilots had an altercation during a flight from Iran to Iraq which broke out into a physical fight at 37,000 feet in July 2018, according to reports at the time, which resulted in both being suspended.

A “violent incident” between two pilots caused a Flydubai aircraft traveling from Dubai, United Arab Emirates to Tel Aviv, Israel to divert to Saudi Arabia this morning, sources told CNN.

Here’s what we know about the situation so far:

The aircraft descended 17,400 feet over northwestern Saudi Arabia in just under two minutes at around 1:20 a.m. ET, flight tracking data reviewed by CNN shows. The plane transmitted an emergency signal at 1:32 a.m. ET.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has held consultations over the aviation incident, his office said today, adding that the situation was “under control.”

Flydubai confirmed that one of its aircraft “experienced an incident,” adding that the plane landed safely in Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk Airport (TUU) and all passengers are safe and accounted for.

Israel is exploring the possibility of sending a plane to Saudi Arabia to bring home passengers who landed there after the diversion, an Israeli official told CNN.

CNN’s Sophie Tanno and Kim Kelaita contributed to this reporting.

The emergency landing of an Israel-bound flight in Saudi Arabia marked a rare mass arrival of Israelis in the kingdom, which has no diplomatic relations with Israel.

Just a few years ago, Israeli airlines and Israel-bound flights were forbidden from even entering Saudi airspace, forcing Israeli holidaymakers to take an hours long detour while traveling east to avoid the vast kingdom.

That changed in 2022, when Riyadh unilaterally allowed Israeli flights to use its airspace as part of a push by the Biden administration to normalize ties between the two countries. It was a milestone for Israeli aviation, significantly shortening routes to Asia, and what allowed Wednesday’s Dubai-Tel Aviv flight to fly over Saudi Arabia.

This wasn’t the first time scores of Israelis unexpectedly landed in the kingdom. In 2023, a Tel Aviv-bound Air Seychelles flight made an emergency landing in the Saudi Red Sea city of Jeddah because of an electrical problem, forcing passengers to stay at an airport hotel. And last year, another Flydubai plane landed in the Saudi capital Riyadh after a passenger suffered a stroke.

Such incidents have been seen as rare signs of Saudi-Israeli cooperation, even as formal normalization remains out of reach.

The Gaza war and its devastating humanitarian toll have hardened Saudi Arabia’s position on recognizing Israel. Riyadh says it will not establish diplomatic relations without the creation of an independent Palestinian state.

Israel is exploring the possibility of sending a plane to Saudi Arabia to bring home passengers who landed there after the diversion of an Israel-bound flight, an Israeli official told CNN.

The plane could be a military or civilian plane of Israel’s national EI AI airline.
