articles.title: More survivors and victims found after boat carrying 62 capsizes near Puerto Rico
articles.summary: The U.S. Coast Guard said it had rescued 49 people and was searching for 10 others after a boat carrying migrants recently capsized in open waters west of Puerto Rico.
articles.body: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — The U.S. Coast Guard said Tuesday it had rescued 49 people and was searching for 10 others after a boat carrying migrants recently capsized in open waters west of Puerto Rico. At least three bodies have been recovered since the boat, carrying 62 passengers, overturned late Sunday near Mona Island. Officials said one passenger attacked others with a machete, causing severe injuries and forcing dozens to jump into the water. U.S. Coast Guard spokesperson Ricardo Castrodad said in a phone interview Tuesday that the majority of people aboard the boat were migrants from the Dominican Republic, while two are believed to be from Haiti. He said he didn’t know what prompted the attack, which “created a situation of panic.” Castrodad said the number of victims could have been much higher if it weren’t for a vessel passing through the area on Monday afternoon that reported the incident and helped rescue four people. “Everyone could have easily died,” he said. Helicopters hovered over Mona Island and nearby areas on Tuesday as rescuers searched for the missing. A Coast Guard video showed at least two survivors wearing life jackets walking along the edge of the rocky island, with one jumping into the water toward a rescuer as waves slapped against the outcrop. It is the latest deadly voyage involving a makeshift vessel attempting to cross the treacherous Mona Passage that separates Puerto Rico from the island of Hispaniola, which is shared by Haiti and the Dominican Republic. Migrants fleeing poverty and violence have long made that journey. In June 2022, 11 Haitian girls and women died after the grossly overloaded boat they were in capsized in open waters northwest of Puerto Rico.

articles.title: Tennessee set to execute a woman for the first time in two centuries
articles.summary: Death row inmate Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, is due to be executed by lethal injection in Tennessee on ​Wednesday, becoming the first woman that state has put to death in more than two hundred years.
articles.body: Death row inmate Christa Pike, convicted of murdering a schoolmate three decades ago, is due to be executed by lethal injection in Tennessee on ​Wednesday, becoming the first woman that state has put to death in more than two hundred years. Pike, whose clemency petition highlighting childhood ‌trauma and sexual abuse was denied by Governor Bill Lee, would also be the only person in the modern era of U.S. capital punishment to be executed in Tennessee for a crime committed as a teenager. The Supreme Court on Tuesday rejected an 11th-hour bid for a stay of execution, which is set to take place at the Riverbend Maximum ​Security Institution in Nashville, the state capital. Pike, now 50, was 18 in January 1995 when she, a 17-year-old boyfriend and a third companion lured ​19-year-old Colleen Slemmer, a classmate at their Knoxville Job Corps vocational center, into a wooded area where they tortured ⁠and killed her. The grisly nature of the slaying, which involved the perpetrators carving the shape of a pentagram in the victim’s chest and taking a chunk ​of her skull as a souvenir of the carnage, drew intense media coverage at the time. Trial testimony indicated that Pike viewed Slemmer as a rival for the ​affections of her boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp. Pike and Shipp confessed to the killing, and both were convicted the following year of first-degree murder. Pike was sentenced to death, while Shipp received a life sentence with the possibility of parole. Their co-defendant, Shadolla Peterson, who was 18 at the time of the murder and had acted as a lookout for the other two, ​appeared as a witness for the prosecution and received probation. Currently the only woman on Tennessee’s death row, Pike was also convicted in August 2001 of ​attempted first-degree murder in an assault on another inmate, according to the Tennessee Department of Correction. In a 226-page petition asking the governor to commute her death penalty to a life ‌sentence without ⁠the possibility of parole, her lawyers documented her history as the childhood victim of violence, neglect and sexual abuse, including two rapes at ages 11 and 17. And they cited the diagnoses she received in prison for bipolar disorder and post-traumatic stress disorder. Teen who committed murder ‘no longer exists’ Her lawyers also pointed to evidence that Pike’s mother drank heavily during pregnancy, contributing to faulty brain development that made it difficult for their client to control her impulses as a young ​person. “The 18-year-old girl suffering from severe mental ​illness and near-debilitating trauma no longer ⁠exists,” her lawyers wrote in response to Lee’s denial of clemency. “Christa is a 50-year-old remorseful woman who understands her actions, receives proper treatment for her mental illness, and provides for and guides fellow incarcerated women.” Slemmer’s mother, May Martinez, has ​spoken out in support of the execution. Executions of female prison inmates are exceedingly rare in the U.S., with women ​accounting for just ⁠18 of the 1,683 people put to death since the Supreme Court allowed capital punishment to resume in 1976, according to the Death Penalty Information Center. Before Wednesday, Tennessee had executed 17 people. Pike’s case has drawn international attention, with a group of United Nations human rights experts issuing a recent statement calling for commutation of her ⁠death sentence. Sexual ​violence and trauma experts have also spoken out on her behalf, arguing that the procedures surrounding ​lethal injection would likely cause Pike to experience severe, traumatic flashbacks of child sexual abuse and rape, adding to the cruelty and anguish of her death. Tennessee prison officials in May aborted attempts to ​execute a man convicted of murders after failing to find a suitable vein for a lethal injection.

articles.title: Israel-bound flight makes emergency landing in Saudi Arabia amid accounts of a bloody onboard altercation
articles.summary: A passenger plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, with witness accounts describing a bloody onboard altercation that forced the flight to make a sudden and extreme descent.
articles.body: A passenger plane from Dubai to Tel Aviv made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday, with witness accounts describing a bloody onboard altercation that forced the flight to make a sudden and extreme descent. Cluster2, which operates at several airports across Saudi Arabia, said both the captain and the first officer of Flydubai Flight 1073 were injured and taken to a hospital after landing. The Israeli military said it scrambled at least two jets in response to the incident, and had not ruled out the possibility that it was terrorism-related. Video from onboard the Boeing 737 appeared to show two people lying on the floor, visibly bloodied as others crowd around them. Motti Cohen Or, a passenger of the flight, told NBC News that he heard a woman shouting, “Someone is stabbing someone in the cockpit.” The plane then started shaking, with the aircraft briefly diving “toward the ground,” Cohen Or, 70, from central Israel, said. Someone then broke into the cockpit and said both the pilot and co-pilot had been stabbed, he added. An assailant was subdued and a pilot who was onboard was able to “take control” of the plane, Cohen Or said. NBC News was not immediately able to independently verify his account. Israeli media, including The Times of Israel and Ynet, cited unidentified security officials as saying that the alert was triggered after an altercation between the plane’s two pilots. The mother of another passenger told NBC News that her daughter had feared for her life as the plane “started to go down and to shake.” Yasmin Abukasis said her daughter, Miriam Shira, said a pilot had been wounded, and that one of the pilots had a knife. NBC News was not immediately able to independently confirm details of the incident. Abukasis said her daughter had described the ordeal as “crazy, like a movie.” A spokesperson for Flydubai said Flight FZ 1073 had “experienced an incident while en route” from Dubai International Airport to Ben Gurion International Airport. The aircraft landed safely at the Prince Sultan bin Abdulaziz International Airport, known as Tabuk Airport, they said. The airline was working to secure a replacement aircraft, and investigators were looking into what happened onboard. The Flydubai flight initially triggered a 7700 “general emergency” signal, aviation tracking site Flightradar24 reported. It then switched to a 7500 code, suggesting “unlawful interference,” before switching back to a 7700, the tracking site said. It said “extreme fluctuations” were observed in the altitude data transmitted from the flight, which appeared to drop by 14,125 feet in just 29 seconds, according to Flightradar24. A spokesperson for the Israel Airports Authority said in a statement that it had opened a waiting and information area at Ben Gurion Airport for passengers’ families. The spokesperson said family members would continue to be updated “as the situation develops.” Earlier, U.S. Ambassador to Israel Mike Huckabee expressed relief in a post on X that the incident didn’t turn out to be “more serious.” “This had everyone in the Middle East (esp Israel) on FULL ALERT this morning,” he said. “Having pilots inflight detouring to ‘fist city’ not your ordinary experience.” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s office said he held consultations on the matter and had monitored developments. “The situation is under control, and all measures are currently being taken to bring the Israeli passengers back to Israel safely,” his office said Wednesday.

articles.title: Flydubai passenger says co-pilot stabbed captain before terrifying plunge, emergency landing
articles.summary: A passenger says a Flydubai co-pilot stabbed the captain before the Israel-bound flight plunged, triggering hijacking fears and an emergency diversion.
articles.body: A Flydubai passenger said the co-pilot apparently stabbed the captain during a cockpit altercation before the Israel-bound jet plunged thousands of feet, triggering a terrifying scene aboard the aircraft and an emergency diversion to Saudi Arabia Wednesday. Two Israeli officials told Reuters that the co-pilot was believed to have stabbed the captain before cabin crew entered the cockpit and took control of the plane. The officials said Israel's current assessment was that the incident may have been an attempted "terror attack." The Jerusalem Post separately reported that the growing assessment among Israel's security establishment, including the IDF, Mossad and Shin Bet, was that the incident was intended as an act of terror. The passenger told Fox News that accounts of what happened remained conflicting, but said passengers understood that the co-pilot had stabbed the captain and then collapsed onto the controls. "There are many different accounts, but apparently the co-pilot stabbed the captain and collapsed onto the controls, shutting down the entire instrument panel. We began plunging downward for several minutes. Everyone on the plane was screaming, the overhead compartments opened, and the power went out. We were sure we were going to die. It was very scary," the passenger said. Flydubai has not publicly confirmed the reported stabbing or the circumstances surrounding the cockpit confrontation. Saudi Arabia's Tabuk airport said both pilots were hospitalized after suffering injuries, according to Reuters. An investigation into the incident remains underway. MIDAIR SCARE FORCES PACKED PASSENGER JET INTO EMERGENCY LANDING, TRAVELERS HOSPITALIZED The Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, and everyone aboard was reported safe, according to officials. A regional official briefed on the incident said an altercation broke out in the cockpit and apparently involved the pilots, though it was not immediately clear what sparked the confrontation. Israeli media, citing security officials, also reported that a dispute between the two pilots was behind the emergency. "The crew have been questioned as part of the investigation," the regional official said, according to The Associated Press, without saying whether anyone had been detained. The incident prompted an immediate security response in Israel, where authorities initially feared the plane — carrying more than 100 Israeli passengers, according to The Jerusalem Post — could have been hijacked. Israel scrambled fighter jets as the situation unfolded. AMERICANS WARNED AGAINST TRAVEL PLANS AS TERRORISM THREATENS POPULAR DESTINATION The aircraft transmitted an emergency alert during the flight, according to publicly available flight-tracking information. Flight FZ1073 had departed Dubai and was headed for Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv before diverting to Tabuk. Flightradar24 data showed the aircraft suddenly plunging nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds before the first emergency signal, according to Reuters. Capt. Meidan Barr, former chairman of the Israel Airline Pilot Association, told Fox News Channel that such a rapid loss of altitude would ordinarily resemble an emergency descent, such as one performed following a loss of cabin pressure. "Losing like 15,000 feet in two or three minutes, that is something that you do in, like, an emergency descent when you lose pressure," Barr said, adding that the aircraft's safe landing was significant and would allow investigators to determine what went wrong. Flight-tracking data also showed the aircraft transmitting emergency transponder code 7700 before briefly switching to 7500, a code used to signal unlawful interference with an aircraft, and later returning to 7700. Passengers described a tense scene aboard the aircraft as the emergency unfolded. Travelers told Israel's Channel 12 by phone that they heard shouting from passengers near the front of the plane who had apparently heard the cockpit altercation. They also said the aircraft dipped steeply before landing in Saudi Arabia. IRISH SOCCER PLAYERS WEAR BLACK ARMBANDS, REFUSE TO SHAKE HANDS AHEAD OF CONTENTIOUS MATCH VS ISRAEL The account provided directly to Fox News offered a more harrowing description of the sudden descent, with the passenger saying people screamed as overhead compartments opened and power aboard the aircraft went out. After landing, passengers remained aboard the plane as a heavy Saudi security presence surrounded the aircraft, according to their accounts to the Israeli outlet. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's office later said the situation was under control and that Israeli authorities were working to bring the passengers home. The scare came as Netanyahu has warned in recent days about unspecified heightened security threats facing Israel. Netanyahu convened security consultations over the incident and cleared the remainder of his schedule to manage the crisis, according to Reuters. The Jerusalem Post reported that Israeli airspace was temporarily closed before reopening after the aircraft landed in Saudi Arabia. Flydubai later confirmed that FZ1073 had experienced an incident while traveling to Ben Gurion Airport and landed safely in Tabuk. "Our teams are working closely with the relevant authorities," the carrier said. "Further updates will be issued as additional confirmed details become available." The exact circumstances surrounding the reported cockpit confrontation remained unclear Wednesday. Flydubai has not publicly confirmed the reported stabbing or provided details about what led to the cockpit confrontation. While disputes between pilots serious enough to affect a flight are rare, similar incidents have occurred. Two Air France pilots were suspended in 2022 after fighting in the cockpit during a flight from Geneva to Paris. That aircraft did not divert and landed as scheduled. The initial hijacking fears carried particular weight in Israel, where aviation security has long been shaped by a history of attacks on Israeli travelers and aircraft. Palestinian militants carried out a series of hijackings and attacks involving Israelis during the 1960s and 1970s. Israel has not experienced an aircraft hijacking in decades and maintains stringent security procedures for Israel-bound flights. Flights between Israel and the United Arab Emirates began after the two countries normalized relations in 2020, opening the UAE as a major destination for Israeli travelers. articles.title: A New York man allegedly began withdrawing money from his brother’s account the day after his death while Social Security remained unaware he had died; prosecutors say the continuing payments ultimately reached $109,746

articles.body: A New York man allegedly began withdrawing money from his deceased brother’s bank account just one day after his death, prosecutors said, as Social Security payments continued to flow into the account because the agency had not yet been notified of the death. The withdrawals and continuing benefit payments eventually amounted to $109,746 in allegedly stolen Social Security benefits, according to the US Department of Justice.The case involving David Darling, of the Northern District of New York, was among 17 cases announced by the Justice Department as part of a month-long enforcement push targeting alleged fraud involving Social Security benefits. According to an indictment cited by the DOJ, Darling had control of his deceased brother’s ATM card and began withdrawing money from the account the day after his brother died. The Social Security Administration was unaware of the death and continued depositing benefits into the account.How the alleged scheme unfoldedThe DOJ's account indicates that the case centred on continued access to an account belonging to a person who had died. After his brother's death, Darling allegedly had possession or control of the brother's ATM card. Prosecutors say he began making withdrawals almost immediately, starting the day after the death.Because the Social Security Administration had not yet learned that the beneficiary had died, payments continued to be deposited into the account.The indictment alleges that Darling then continued withdrawing money from the account, ultimately resulting in $109,746 in Social Security benefits being identified as stolen.The DOJ has charged Darling with three federal offences: access device fraud, theft of government property and aggravated identity theft.An indictment is an accusation, and the charges against Darling are allegations. He is presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty in court.Three federal chargesAccording to the Justice Department, the charges carry different potential penalties. The access-device-fraud charge, brought under 18 U.S. Code § 1029, can carry a maximum sentence of up to 15 years in prison in the circumstances outlined by prosecutors.The theft-of-government-property charge under 18 U.S. Code § 641 carries a maximum penalty of up to 10 years, according to the DOJ.Darling also faces an aggravated identity-theft charge under 18 U.S. Code § 1028A. The DOJ said that offence carries a mandatory minimum sentence of two years in prison.The case is being prosecuted by Assistant US Attorney Arne Soldwedel for the Northern District of New York, with Assistant US Attorney Benjamin Clark serving as District Fraud Counsel adviser, the department said.For Darling, however, the allegations will now have to be tested in federal court.Wider Social Security fraud crackdownDarling's case was one of several announced by the Justice Department on September 29 as part of a surge of criminal enforcement actions involving Social Security Administration benefit programs, including Supplemental Security Income.Between August 21 and September 18, the DOJ's National Fraud Enforcement Division and US attorneys in 11 federal districts, with assistance from the Social Security Administration's Office of Inspector General, brought charges against 17 defendants.The department said those cases represented more than $1.3 million in intended losses to the United States. The cases involved a range of alleged schemes, including the misuse of benefits belonging to deceased people, representative-payee fraud and alleged identity theft.One Illinois case involved a woman prosecutors allege concealed her mother's body in a garage freezer for two years while assuming her mother's identity and collecting her Social Security and other benefits. The DOJ put the intended loss in that case at $21,402.In another case from Pennsylvania, prosecutors allege that a woman continued taking her deceased father's Social Security retirement payments after his death in November 2020. The department said payments continued until October 2023, with $59,070 allegedly stolen.Other cases announced as part of the enforcement effort involved alleged misuse of benefits belonging to elderly or disabled recipients. The Social Security Administration's Office of Inspector General assisted the Justice Department in the wider enforcement operation, which covered 11 federal districts.You use AI every day. articles.title: Plans to demolish Haven Hotel in Sandbanks rejected
articles.summary: Bournemouth Christchurch and Poole Council said the application for Haven Hotel lacked information.
articles.body:
Plans to demolish a seaside hotel have been rejected, after a council said the developer "failed to provide sufficient information" about the works.

The Haven Hotel, built in 1887 and expanded in the 1920s, sits on the southern corner of Sandbanks, at the entrance to Poole Harbour in Dorset.

Bournemouth Christchurch and Poole Council (BCP) said the application for prior approval by Planning Strategy Ltd lacked key information on the demolition process, site restoration and environmental impacts.

Council planners said they could not properly assess the potential effects on neighbouring properties, local residents and the environment.

In the application to BCP by Pure Town Planning, on behalf of Planning Strategy, it stated: "demolition and the securing of the site is the responsible course," and that "no justification for the demolition is required".

It added: "A large vacant building in this exposed and highly visible coastal location would be vulnerable to unauthorised entry, vandalism and the breakage of glazing, with consequent harm to the visual amenity of a prominent seafront frontage and a risk to public safety.

Haven Hotel continues to operate on the site.

The application for the 2.5-acre site, was met by more than 50 objections.

It followed previous plans by FJB Hotels and developer Fortitudo, to replace the hotel with flats, which were refused in 2022.

More than 6,000 people objected to the previous scheme, which also included plans to replace Sandbanks Hotel with a 171-room hotel and Harbour Heights Hotel with 38 hotel apartments.

The Sandbanks Community Group, which has consistently opposed proposals at the site has said it is "delighted" with the BCP's decision.

It said "enough is enough" adding that it would support the owner of the site so that it can remain a "top class hotel".

articles.summary: A victory for Lula would strengthen authoritarian regimes, undermining democracy and the United States’ strategy under the new Monroe Doctrine.

In recent years, the radical left has lost almost every election in Latin America. However, in Brazil, President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva — an ally of China , Russia and Iran — is attempting to win a fourth term in Sunday’s election.

Some 160 million Brazilians will head to the polls to elect a president, governors and legislative representatives. Sen. Flavio Bolsonaro — son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, who was unjustly imprisoned — is in a virtual dead heat with President Lula, and a runoff election is considered likely.

These are no ordinary elections. Brazil is the largest country in Latin America and plays a pivotal role bridging the Western democracies of the G20 and the so-called Global South within the BRICS group featuring Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa. He also condemned the alleged blockade against Cuba, defended Palestine and accused the Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu of committing genocide.

His remarks at the U.N. were praised by Khaled Qaddoumi, political representative in Iran of the terrorist group Hamas. In a statement published by Metropolis, Qaddoumi said the Brazilian leader was on the right side of history.

Lula has also insisted that the U.S. dollar should not be the hegemonic currency. He asks that Nicolás Maduro be tried in Venezuela and assures that Cuba is the victim of a massacre fueled by U.S. speculation.

In his efforts to distance himself from the dollar and the U.S., Lula has increased his dependence on China. He also announced that Brazil is moving forward with issuing panda bonds using yuan as currency. In other words, Brazil already sells most of its iron ore , soybeans and oil to Beijing, but now it also wants to borrow using Chinese yuan, limiting its financial freedom to the communist power.

Lula has gone above and beyond. Earlier this year Brazil received with arms wide-open the military hospital ship Silk Road Ark owned by the People’s Liberation Army Navy. Members of the naval forces of both countries conducted a joint maritime exercise on search and rescue. China also made a demonstration of a combat and rescue operation.

In the telecommunications sector, Brazil continues working together with Huawei . The controversial company has been accused of alleged espionage by several European countries and the United States.

Lula has also shown little commitment to combating drug trafficking by declining to join the “Shield of the Americas” initiative and refusing to designate criminal gangs like the Primeiro Comando da Capital and Comando Vermelho as terrorist organizations.

Four more years of Lula would put at risk the crucial relation with America. Brazil is one of the world’s largest economies, and the U.S. is its second-most important trading partner. In 2023, U.S. exports of goods and services to Brazil totaled $37.9 billion, while imports from Brazil amounted to $36.9 billion, representing a total trade value of $74.8 billion.

Brazil needs and deserves a change, and a new leadership that defends democracy, freedom and the rule of law. On Sunday, there is a great chance for a historic resurrection of the largest nation in South America.
